title: Home Service AI Startup Broccoli Forecasts $60M in Annual Revenue
summary:
The founder-led company that provides digital voice and text assistants for residential trade contractors says its business has grown to a booking run rate of more than $1 billion per year for customer jobs. The startup, which helps plumbers and electricians automate lead follow-ups and scheduling, expects to end the year with annual recurring revenue of more than $60 million.

The financial targets follow a combined $52 million in funding for Broccoli's Series A and B rounds, led by Khosla Ventures and Y Combinator. The business was launched in early 2024 by Abhishek Jain and Aditya Ketkar, who developed the AI front-office tools after their previous electric vehicle startup failed to find product-market fit.

selectedTweets.text:
Broccoli (W22) is building an AI front office for home services businesses, answering calls, following up with leads, and booking appointments across voice and text.

Today, they serve more than 500 customers, are booking jobs at a run rate of over $1 billion a year, and expect to end the year at more than $60 million in ARR, up from zero just two years ago, after recently raising a $30 million Series B.  

In this fireside, @call_broccoli's founders @abhishekjain25 and @adityaketkar join YC's @gustaf to share the long path to finding that business, from an earlier EV startup that never found product-market fit to visiting 140 contractors across the Bay Area to understand their biggest problems firsthand. They explain how embedding inside a plumbing company led to the first version of Broccoli, why answering missed calls became the wedge, and how AI could eventually reshape the work of technicians themselves.
